evidence.summary: NVIDIA reported record fiscal Q3 2026 revenue and record data-center revenue, with management commentary indicating very strong AI compute demand.
Amazon said AWS revenue grew 28% year over year in Q1 2026 and disclosed large AI chip deployments and planned NVIDIA GPU rollout.
Amazon said it expects about $200 billion of 2026 capex, explicitly citing AI as a major opportunity.
Arista reported strong 2025 results and highlighted continued momentum in large AI and data-center networking environments.
Vertiv reported strong orders and backlog, with demand particularly strong in AI infrastructure.
Vertiv announced OneCore, a prefabricated infrastructure solution for AI, HPC, and high-density data centers.

memory_update.text: For Layer 3 AI ranking, prioritize the most structurally scarce upstream control points first: accelerators, foundry/advanced packaging, networking, and data-center power/cooling.
Memory/HBM, advanced packaging subcontractors, photonics, and test/inspection equipment remain under-covered and should be added in the next research pass.
Hyperscalers such as Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, and Meta are demand engines rather than bottleneck suppliers; they are useful for validation but should usually rank below scarce-layer suppliers.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need primary-source confirmation of current capacity constraints, shipment timing, and how much incremental demand is already locked versus still opportunistic.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Core AI accelerator supplier at the center of the theme; strongest direct exposure to AI compute demand, with repeated evidence of record data-center revenue and sold-out cloud GPU demand. This is the cleanest public-market proxy for the AI compute bottleneck.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need more direct evidence on AI-related advanced packaging utilization, customer concentration, and whether incremental capacity is already reserved.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Critical foundry and advanced-packaging node for leading-edge AI chips. If AI accelerators keep scaling, wafer and packaging capacity remain a gating layer, making TSM one of the most structurally important names in the chain.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need current order/capacity and regional mix detail to separate secular AI demand from cyclical semiconductor capex.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Lithography remains one of the hardest-to-replicate bottlenecks in leading-edge semiconductor manufacturing. AI-driven wafer demand makes this a key upstream control point with extreme supplier scarcity.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need finer detail on AI-related backlog, customer mix, and whether growth is broadening beyond the largest hyperscaler rollouts.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: High-speed Ethernet switching and data-center networking are a distinct AI bottleneck, separate from compute. Arista has strong evidence of AI networking momentum and is one of the cleanest public-market expressions of cluster buildout.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need more granular evidence on how much of backlog is directly AI-related versus general data-center refresh and how durable margins are under faster capacity expansion.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: AI data-center power and cooling are increasingly binding constraints, especially with higher rack densities and liquid cooling requirements. Vertiv has unusually strong evidence around orders, backlog, and AI-specific infrastructure adaptation.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need clearer separation of AI networking/ASIC revenue from broader semis and better visibility into customer dependence and concentration.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Broadcom sits at the intersection of AI networking and custom silicon/ASIC infrastructure. It is less pure than a single-node bottleneck, but still a major infrastructure enabler with strong strategic importance.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need to quantify how much capex is specifically AI-driven versus broader cloud/infrastructure expansion.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: A major AI demand engine through AWS capex and AI chip deployment, with strong disclosed spending plans. Important for theme confirmation, but not a bottleneck supplier itself.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need more detail on AI capex intensity and whether growth is translating into sustained infrastructure pull-through or mostly software monetization.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Azure and AI deployment make Microsoft a key demand node and a high-quality confirmation source for AI infrastructure spending, but it is not a scarcity point in the chain.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need more precise disclosure on AI infrastructure capex versus broader product and advertising-related spend.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Important AI compute demand driver through model training and data-center expansion. Useful as a demand-side signal, but less directly tied to a scarce supply node than NVDA/TSM/ASML/ANET/VRT.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need more specific AI infrastructure and capex decomposition, plus clearer linkage to downstream supply-chain stress.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Strong AI and cloud demand engine, especially for search/model deployment and Google Cloud. Better for demand validation than for bottleneck discovery.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: AI-specific revenue contribution is not yet well quantified; need direct evidence of order flow tied to data-center/grid buildouts.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Potential AI power-grid beneficiary as data-center electricity demand grows. More indirect than Vertiv, but useful for mapping the power bottleneck beyond IT hardware.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need more direct evidence of AI-linked orders and a tighter split between general electrification demand and AI-specific demand.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Electrical distribution and power-management exposure gives Eaton a real AI infrastructure link, especially around data-center buildouts and grid constraints.

summary: Layer 3 prioritizes the most research-worthy AI theme candidates by combining demand durability, chokepoint severity, supplier scarcity, public-market purity, evidence quality, mispricing potential, falsifiability, and risk clarity. The highest-priority names are the clearest bottleneck/control points in the AI stack: NVIDIA, TSMC, ASML, Arista, Vertiv, and Broadcom. Hyperscalers remain critical demand engines, but they rank lower as bottlenecks because they mostly pull demand rather than constrain supply. Under-covered but important next-step research areas remain memory/HBM, advanced packaging, photonics, and test/inspection equipment.
